bull_bear.body: - ~Rs. 1,000 cr equity raised for BESS. Heavy reinvestment across the full value chain ("Waaree 2.0"). Prudent working-capital posture (advances/full-payment-before-ship). No dividend discussion on call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- US anti-dumping / circumvention investigation (Indonesia/Laos routing) — Rs.294 cr provision booked pre-emptively; outcome unresolved.
- Commodity risk: silver & cell-price inflation (China cells ¢4–4.5 → ~¢6/Wp).
- Cell utilization optics (quarter-avg 56% vs daily 80%) — execution to be proven next quarter.
- Tariff regime "continuously evolving"; reliant on cell country-of-origin rules.
- India PPA logjam (~42 GW stuck) — transmission/transformer/bay/land bottlenecks; demand timing risk.
- New-vertical (BESS/H2/inverter) economics still "embryonic" — no audited numbers.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly promotional, superlative-heavy ("stellar," "record-breaking," "two big dogs"). CEO candid on declining FY27 guidance and on US-investigation provisioning. CFO precise and numbers-fluent. A mid-call audio glitch occurred; mgmt compensated with extra time. Confident, slightly salesy.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The China export-rebate taper (pushing cell prices up ~50%) is framed as a *positive* — it "proves up" Chinese costs and makes Indian supply globally competitive.
- US is the margin engine: ¢28–30/Wp realizations dwarf India's ~Rs.18.5/Wp non-DCR; IRA 45X booked conservatively (90% of ¢7, partial volume) — implies hidden upside / cushion.
- Mgmt is deliberately moving away from quoting GW (mix-driven), signaling EPC/turnkey/non-module revenue is becoming material and harder to benchmark.
- Captive cell consumption + rising DCR is the structural margin story, not spot pricing.
- "Overcapacity is a myth" stance: 9M module/cell demand (35 GW) already exceeds full prior-year; bets demand keeps "galloping."
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt to Equity of -0.08x as on 30th June 2026 (i.e. net cash), against a historical series of -0.80 (FY23), -0.85 (FY24), -0.72 (FY25) and -0.29 (FY26); the deck also claims a D/E ratio maintained at <1 'despite heavy capex cycles for nearly a decade'.
- Return ratios of ROCE 28.5% and ROE 24.8%, both on trailing-12-month numbers and adjusted for the unutilized portion of IPO proceeds.
- Capital allocation is governed by a stated 'book & build' principle — 'Before commissioning US facility, secured 3+ years of firm orders' and 'Cell capex initiated post long-term orders and policy visibility' — with expansion 'backed by strong order visibility' and described as ROCE and ROE accretive.
- Funding of the ₹31,497 Cr programme is stated to come from strong operating cash flow, customer advances and a significant cash balance, with capital de-risking via central and state subsidies including PLI.
- The certifications slide carries a 'CREDIT RATING UPGRADED TO' header, but the rating itself did not survive extraction (see notes).

- scale: largest solar module manufacturer in India and the largest non-Chinese module maker globally — evidence: ~25.8 GW of solar module manufacturing capacity across 36 production lines; PV module production of 9,840 MW in FY 2025-26 (Board's Report); Waaree has the highest share of India's 14.3% of global module shipments (JMK Research)
- integration: in-house solar cell supply for its own modules — evidence: 5.4 GW solar cell capacity on 11 lines at Chikhli, Gujarat — against it: cell capacity of 5.4 GW sits against ~25.8 GW of module capacity
- integration: upstream ingot-wafer and cell build-out towards a polysilicon-to-module chain — evidence: 10 GW integrated ingot-wafer facility at Nagpur (groundbreaking 14 March 2026, ₹ 6,200 Crores capex, expected commissioning FY2028); 10 GW cell plant under construction at Unn to take cell capacity to 15.4 GW by FY27; board-approved 2,500 TPD solar glass plant (FY29) [planned]
- integration: traceable polysilicon supply outside China — evidence: strategic stake in United Solar Holding Inc., Oman, described as the largest non-Chinese polysilicon manufacturer with 100 KTPA capacity, securing FEOC-compliant polysilicon for US and global markets
- licence/regulatory: US-located module manufacturing aligned to IRA/FEOC frameworks — evidence: 1.6 GW module plant in Texas operational, further 1.6 GW under construction and a 1 GW Meyer Burger asset acquired in Arizona, targeting 4.8 GW of US capacity by FY27 — against it: US Customs and Border Protection has commenced an EAPA investigation into the origin of components in modules the company exported from India to the USA since January 2021
- licence/regulatory: production-linked incentive allocations — evidence: secured 6 GW PLI for integrated manufacturing and a PLI for electrolyser manufacturing (1 GW Dungri electrolyser plant, PLI awarded)
- distribution: nationwide retail channel for rooftop and small-system solar — evidence: 700+ franchisees, 2,500+ authorised selling partners, presence in 27 states, ~15,000 pincodes and 5,000+ MNRE integrators on its loyalty app
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US Customs (CBP) EAPA investigation into module origin — The Board's Report discloses that US Customs and Border Protection formally opened an Enforce and Protect Act investigation against the company and Waaree Solar Americas, Inc. into the origin of components in modules made in India and exported to the USA, and the duties on them, since January 2021. The outcome is pending, and the US is one of the company's main export markets.
- Geopolitical disruption in West Asia and the Strait of Hormuz — The MD&A flags the Middle East conflict as a significant near-term risk to trade flows, energy supply and supply-chain stability, with crude oil prices rising sharply. That feeds into input and logistics costs and material availability for a large manufacturer.
- Input cost and material-availability pressure from the Russia-Ukraine conflict — The MD&A says the protracted conflict keeps weighing on oil supply, commodity prices and logistics networks, which keeps input costs under upward pressure and adds uncertainty about the availability of key materials and services.
- Trade-policy and tariff uncertainty — The MD&A expects economic policy uncertainty around global trade policies and tariffs to stay elevated through 2026, which could dampen investment and trade flows. That matters for an exporter with overseas manufacturing.
- Softer renewable growth forecasts from policy and regulatory shifts — The MD&A notes that the IEA trimmed its 2025-2030 renewable growth forecast by 5%, citing policy shifts, regulatory changes, geopolitical conditions and evolving market dynamics, alongside heightened policy uncertainty and changing regulatory frameworks for the industry.

- Execution speed claimed as a differentiator: module capacity expanded ~17x to 25.8 GW within 7 years 'ahead of schedule', India cell capacity to grow ~3x to 15.4 GW 'in a record time of ~2 years', and 1.6 GW of greenfield US module capacity built in 12 months.

outlook.body:
- Scale: grow manufacturing across polysilicon, ingots-wafers, cells, modules and glass as the largest non-Chinese module manufacturer with an operating US footprint.

outlook.body: During FY26 the company commissioned an additional 4.85 GW of module capacity at Chikhli and 3 GW at Samakhiali (Kutch), Gujarat, taking standalone module capacity to 22.75 GW at 31 March 2026; the manufactured-capital section puts module capacity at ~25.8 GW across 36 lines, with 5.4 GW of cells at Chikhli. The next phase, branded Waaree 2.0 with a ₹ 30,000+ Crores strategic capex roadmap, has several parts. Upstream solar: a 10 GW cell plant under construction at Unn, Gujarat (FY27) to take cell capacity to 15.4 GW; India's largest 10 GW integrated ingot-wafer facility at Nagpur, Maharashtra (groundbreaking March 2026, operational readiness targeted by FY28); a strategic stake in United Solar Holding Inc., Oman for polysilicon; and a board-approved 2,500 TPD solar glass plant in Gujarat (FY29). United States: Texas Phase I (1.6 GW) is operational and Phase II (1.6 GW) is under construction, and an acquired 1 GW Meyer Burger asset in Arizona is being revamped to 1.6 GW, taking US capacity to 4.8 GW by FY27. Adjacencies: the Rola, Gujarat BESS container line (5.15 GWh) is operational, with pack and cell under construction and a roadmap to 20 GWh by FY29; the 1 GW electrolyser plant at Dungri, Gujarat is due in FY27; Sarodhi inverter Phase II (additional 1 GW, to 4 GW) and Alwar transformer Phase II (to 20,000 MVA) are due by FY27; and a further Gujarat plant at Azamnagar is due in FY28. The company entered transformers and smart meters by acquiring companies in those businesses (the transformer maker is now Waaree Transpower, formerly Kotsons), and deployed about ₹ 2,000 Crores in acquisitions and investments.

outlook.body:
- India's renewable capacity continues to scale rapidly with solar leading incremental additions; India targets 280 GW of solar by 2030 under the 500 GW non-fossil goal.
- Policy support — PLI, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM — and localisation measures (Basic Customs Duty, ALMM) favour domestic manufacturers and reduce import dependence.
- Rising electricity demand, industrial decarbonisation, data-centre growth and electrification are expected to accelerate renewable adoption; corporate PPA demand is rising with AI data-centre expansion.
- The Indian solar EPC market is structurally underpenetrated with a shortage of large, credible EPC contractors, which management sees as an opportunity for integrated players to gain share.
- The US is accelerating domestic manufacturing under IRA incentives, but the IEA cut its 2025-2030 renewable forecast by 5%, with the sharpest cuts (nearly 50%) in the US.
- Energy storage integration is emerging as a critical enabler; the CEA estimates India needs 47 GW / 236 GWh of BESS by 2032.
- Domestic PV glass demand is projected to outstrip current domestic capacity, leaving a structural supply gap that creates room for domestic producers.
- Grid modernisation and transmission build-out are driving transformer demand in India.
- The Board's Report says the company sizably improved its order book from major developers during FY26 alongside significant growth in exports to markets like the USA.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's renewable capacity continues to scale rapidly with solar leading incremental additions; India targets 280 GW of solar by 2030 under the 500 GW non-fossil goal.
- Policy support — PLI, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM — and localisation measures (Basic Customs Duty, ALMM) favour domestic manufacturers and reduce import dependence.
- Rising electricity demand, industrial decarbonisation, data-centre growth and electrification are expected to accelerate renewable adoption; corporate PPA demand is rising with AI data-centre expansion.
- The Indian solar EPC market is structurally underpenetrated with a shortage of large, credible EPC contractors, which management sees as an opportunity for integrated players to gain share.
- The US is accelerating domestic manufacturing under IRA incentives, but the IEA cut its 2025-2030 renewable forecast by 5%, with the sharpest cuts (nearly 50%) in the US.
- Energy storage integration is emerging as a critical enabler; the CEA estimates India needs 47 GW / 236 GWh of BESS by 2032.
- Domestic PV glass demand is projected to outstrip current domestic capacity, leaving a structural supply gap that creates room for domestic producers.
- Grid modernisation and transmission build-out are driving transformer demand in India.
- The Board's Report says the company sizably improved its order book from major developers during FY26 alongside significant growth in exports to markets like the USA.

The next phase, branded Waaree 2.0 with a ₹ 30,000+ Crores strategic capex roadmap, has several parts. Upstream solar: a 10 GW cell plant under construction at Unn, Gujarat (FY27) to take cell capacity to 15.4 GW; India's largest 10 GW integrated ingot-wafer facility at Nagpur, Maharashtra (groundbreaking March 2026, operational readiness targeted by FY28); a strategic stake in United Solar Holding Inc., Oman for polysilicon; and a board-approved 2,500 TPD solar glass plant in Gujarat (FY29). growth verticals / optionality:
- **Inverters:** 3 GW Sarodhi (Gujarat) phase-1 commissioned; +1 GW phase-2 by FY27. India inverter market ~4x by 2035.
- **Transformers:** expanding to 20,000 MVA, Capex ~Rs.192 cr; order book Rs.245 cr incl. a global MNC order.
- **BESS:** 20 GWh facility ready by FY28; indigenizing anode/cathode/electrolyte; ~$1 bn capex → ~$1.5–2 bn potential revenue (1.5–2x asset turn); first 10 MW pilot order taken.
- **Green hydrogen:** 1 GW electrolyser, Capex ~Rs.676 cr, live by FY27, PLI Rs.444 cr.
- **Renewable power infra:** PPAs 713 MW signed; 6.1 GW connectivity secured; ~3,500 acres acquired + ~13,500 acres under acquisition (≈5–6 GW land). Full-stack platform sold to infra funds/PE who lack land-aggregation mandate.
- Raised ~Rs. 1,000 cr equity for the 20 GWh battery facility.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Gross margin managed via back-to-back cell tying; commodity risk avoided where possible (pass-through is contract-dependent — "sometimes on us").
- Silver impact <9% on a module basis; silver ~25% of cell cost.
- India cell cost of production ~¢7/Wp now (scale benefits to come).
- Realizations: non-DCR module ~Rs.18.5/Wp (India non-DCR ~Rs.14–15; US ~Rs.24–25+); DCR module ~Rs.23–24/Wp.
- Margin levers: rising DCR content, daily utilization gains, operating leverage, price hikes if needed. Mgmt commits to holding/improving margins despite peers (RenewSys/Jackson) flagging need for ~25% price hikes.
capex / expansion:
- All of modules, cells, ingots & wafers to be operationalized by FY27.
- New 10 GW cell facility: ~4 months per line ramp (first lines ~6 months) given 5.4 GW learning curve.
- 10 GW ingot & wafer (FY27): crystal-puller sourcing diversified beyond China; restrictions eased; in negotiations (won't disclose vendors). ASM Technologies & Rana Semiconductor noted by analyst as Indian equipment makers.
capital allocation: - ~Rs. 1,000 cr equity raised for BESS. Heavy reinvestment across the full value chain ("Waaree 2.0"). Prudent working-capital posture (advances/full-payment-before-ship). No dividend discussion on call.
risks & watch-items:
- US anti-dumping / circumvention investigation (Indonesia/Laos routing) — Rs.294 cr provision booked pre-emptively; outcome unresolved.
- Commodity risk: silver & cell-price inflation (China cells ¢4–4.5 → ~¢6/Wp).
- Cell utilization optics (quarter-avg 56% vs daily 80%) — execution to be proven next quarter.
- Tariff regime "continuously evolving"; reliant on cell country-of-origin rules.
- India PPA logjam (~42 GW stuck) — transmission/transformer/bay/land bottlenecks; demand timing risk.
- New-vertical (BESS/H2/inverter) economics still "embryonic" — no audited numbers.
management quality / tone: Highly promotional, superlative-heavy ("stellar," "record-breaking," "two big dogs"). CEO candid on declining FY27 guidance and on US-investigation provisioning. CFO precise and numbers-fluent. A mid-call audio glitch occurred; mgmt compensated with extra time. Confident, slightly salesy.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The China export-rebate taper (pushing cell prices up ~50%) is framed as a *positive* — it "proves up" Chinese costs and makes Indian supply globally competitive.
- US is the margin engine: ¢28–30/Wp realizations dwarf India's ~Rs.18.5/Wp non-DCR; IRA 45X booked conservatively (90% of ¢7, partial volume) — implies hidden upside / cushion.
- Mgmt is deliberately moving away from quoting GW (mix-driven), signaling EPC/turnkey/non-module revenue is becoming material and harder to benchmark.
- Captive cell consumption + rising DCR is the structural margin story, not spot pricing.
- "Overcapacity is a myth" stance: 9M module/cell demand (35 GW) already exceeds full prior-year; bets demand keeps "galloping."

themes.title: Solar PV cell-to-module manufacturing
themes.need: Solar module/cell manufacturers ride capacity ramp, ALMM/DCR protection and an order-book build-out - a manufacturing thesis distinct from firm-power/FDRE tender economics or merchant storage arbitrage. Q1FY27 quantified the DCR arbitrage: EMMVEE grew revenue 51% to INR 1,555cr with EBITDA margin up to 35.2% and PAT +103% on a 9.9 GW order book, with DCR modules earning INR 8.5-9/W of EBITDA against INR 2-2.5/W for non-DCR - a 3-4x per-watt gap that structurally separates integrated cell makers from module assemblers. The offset is order timing: SWSOLAR booked a record INR 13,000cr unexecuted order value on a landmark USD 560m Egypt win (1,000 MW solar + 600 MWh BESS) yet revenue still fell 10% YoY, and flagged that industry orders concluded only ~INR 6,400cr against the >INR 20,000cr expected, deferred by DCR/module-price uncertainty.
themes.driver: DCR cell/module capacity commissioning and the ALMM List-2 per-watt spread; domestic ordering restarting after two slow quarters (SWSOLAR); order-book conversion.
